## Primary research and decision

- Reader question: why can a Linux pathname syscall be observed independently while a correctly attached eBPF per-syscall program emits no AgentSight mutation SUMMARY?
- Source fact: [product master change](https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/agentsight/commit/fbc6d91a025b561970f6e526a5c77bb07754f30a) reports a CI case with all pathname programs entered zero times while FD-oriented hooks aggregated; changes seven pathname-specific `tp/syscalls/sys_enter_*` programs into one `tp/raw_syscalls/sys_enter` dispatcher, then verifies expected summary *types* in a root-only runtime fixture. The change is **not in stable v1.0.35**.
- Independent source cross-check: [Linux `kernel/trace/trace_syscalls.c` at `4843f6873f7c4835e62f2c73ba0fd538e57a2f22`](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/4843f6873f7c4835e62f2c73ba0fd538e57a2f22/kernel/trace/trace_syscalls.c) contains faultable user-buffer metadata/handling, yet its `perf_syscall_enter` calls the BPF program before allocating/filling perf-event buffers. It does **not** prove the original CI explanation generalizes to every kernel; preserve its uncertainty and kernel-version sensitivity. A product-specific regression was reported, not independently reproduced here.
- Additional source caveat: [`bpf/process.c`](https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/agentsight/blob/fbc6d91a025b561970f6e526a5c77bb07754f30a/bpf/process.c) prints both `phase=start` and `phase=exit` `FS_LINK_INFO` immediately after attach, so the second label is not an actual shutdown measurement; previously identified on November 21. Relevant for probe-lifecycle diagnosis.
- Information gain: original five-gate tracepoint delivery/dispatcher/PID scope/user-buffer/aggregate-flush diagnostic map; architecture- and offset-specific syscall dispatch table; verified kernel-order nuance that prevents an overconfident kernel explanation; read-only reproducibility workflow and diagnostic caveats. Distinct from existing [/blog/what-agentsight-filesystem-mutation-summaries-mean/](https://agentsight.us/blog/what-agentsight-filesystem-mutation-summaries-mean/) (interpret *present* SUMMARY and syscall outcomes), [/blog/how-agentsight-reports-capture-loss/](https://agentsight.us/blog/how-agentsight-reports-capture-loss/) (post-probe lost TLS/event data), and [/blog/what-agentsight-file-open-events-prove/](https://agentsight.us/blog/what-agentsight-file-open-events-prove/) (successful file-open evidence). A separate canonical addresses *probe delivery diagnosis*, not a keyword swap.
- Proposed route: `/blog/why-pathname-syscall-probes-can-miss-events/`. Includes source-pinned TechArticle, verification/limits, appropriate internal links. Rendered scope: one new article, one Blog/CollectionPage card, one sitemap canonical/lastmod. Non-rendered scope: this daily record and status. Preserve every previous page, site analytics, workflows, protected control plane, private exports and recurring operations schedule.
